findings.evidence: Artin.lean:139-141 `def indVirtualCharacterSpan (P) := AddSubgroup.closure {f | ∃ χ ∈ indCharacterSet k G {C | P C}, (χ : G → k) = f}`; Spanning.lean:233-235 `def indCharacterSet (𝒮) := {f | ∃ S ∈ 𝒮, ∃ n ρ, ρ.IsIrreducible ∧ ind S (ofCharacter ρ) = f}`; Ideal.lean:80-90 `indVirtualCharacterSet`/`indVirtualCharacters` use `∃ ψ ∈ virtualCharacters k S, indClassFun S ψ = u`; Artin.lean:297-301 proves the equality only under `[IsAlgClosed k]` and `hP : ∀ C, P C → IsUnit (Nat.card C : k)`.
findings.fix: Name the definition after its actual generators, following the file's own `indCharacterSet`/`indCharacterSpan` pair: e.g. `indIrreducibleCharacterSpan` (or `indCharacterAddSpan`, since it is the `AddSubgroup` counterpart of `indCharacterSpan` over the same generating set). Rename the dependent lemmas accordingly (`ind_ofCharacter_mem_…`, `…_le_iff`, `indVirtualCharacterSpan_le_indVirtualCharacters`, `indVirtualCharacters_le_indVirtualCharacterSpan`, `indVirtualCharacters_eq_indVirtualCharacterSpan`) plus the module-docstring entries in Artin.lean:37.
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharacterSpan k G P` is the ℤ-span of characters induced from *irreducible* characters (`AddSubgroup.closure {f | ∃ χ ∈ indCharacterSet k G {C | P C}, ↑χ = f}`), but its name says "span of induced virtual characters", which is exactly what `indVirtualCharacters k G P` (Ideal.lean:89, closure of `indClassFun S ψ` for `ψ ∈ virtualCharacters k S`) already denotes. The two are different definitions, equal only under `IsAlgClosed k` and order invertibility. Consequently `indVirtualCharacterSpan_le_indVirtualCharacters` (line 246) and `indVirtualCharacters_eq_indVirtualCharacterSpan` (line 297) read as trivialities, hiding that the latter carries real hypotheses, and a user choosing between the two names by meaning cannot tell them apart.

summary: The new definition `indVirtualCharacterSpan` names an object whose generators are induced irreducible characters, but the name is one letter and a suffix away from `indVirtualCharacters`, which is the (provably different) subgroup generated by induced virtual characters; the resulting comparison lemmas read as tautologies. All other new names and the bundled-map lemma suffixes are correct.
